title: pane.wait
description: Waits on the caller's own pane, or one it spawned, until its shell finishes a command, draws its next prompt, its program writes anything, a later line matches a pattern or the program is quiet for a while, or the pane closes, or the timeout passes. Needs hello version 2 and a caller in a pane; a pane it did not spawn is refused. At most 64 waits are parked in the core at once, and past that a wait is refused as busy. A wait whose connection closes is dropped.

pane.description: "self", or the number of the caller's own pane or one it spawned. Other panes are refused.

until.description: exit: OSC 133 D. prompt: OSC 133 A. output: any bytes from the program. match: a line printed after the wait began, as plain text without escape sequences, matches pattern. Each finished line is tried once, keeping its newest 64 KiB, and the newest 4 KiB of the line being printed is tried as it grows. On a pane other than the caller's own, the pattern sees only the redacted line, so it cannot probe a secret. idle: the program writes nothing for idle_ms. Output can fake the marks.

pattern.description: With match only, and required there: a regex in the Rust regex crate's syntax, at most 1024 bytes, matched in linear time. One that compiles to more than 64 KiB is refused.

idle_ms.description: With idle only, and required there.

outcome.description: What ended the wait. A timeout is a result, not an error.

exit.description: With exit only: the status the shell gave in its D mark, or null if it gave none.

line.description: With match only: the line that matched, without its line end. Redacted, as it was matched, unless the pane is the caller's own.
